examples.knowledge_point: Differentiating the Product of a Constant and the Exponential Function, Plus a Constant
examples.worked_solution:
The derivative of $e^x$ is just $e^x$ itself. On the other hand, $\ln 3$ is a constant, so its derivative is $0.$

Using the addition rule, then, we have 

$$
\eqalign{
f'(x) &= \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(3e^x + \ln 3\right)\
                                                  &= \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left( 3e^x\right) +  \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left( \ln 3 \right)\
                                                  &= 3\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(e^x\right) + 0\
                                                  &= 3 e^x.
}
$$
